title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your assistant's context window is large enough to hold every student record. A student chats on Monday, and the session ends. On Thursday a new session starts with no extra code. What does the model know about Monday?

options.text: Everything, because the large window keeps all earlier chats stored
Nothing, because a new session begins with an empty context window
A summary, because the model compacts old sessions on its own
Only tool results, because tool outputs are kept by the model

items.stem: A 400-page manual set is searched before each answer. Which design keeps cost per request lowest while still answering from the manuals?

options.text: Search a chunk index and put only the best few chunks in context
Paste all manuals into the instructions so every call can see them
Let the model answer from training and skip the manuals entirely
Paste the manuals in once and rely on the model to remember them

items.stem: In one sentence: why does each later step of an agent loop usually cost more than the earlier steps?
The assistant must know on Thursday that a student passed 3D printer training on Monday. Which is the right mechanism?

options.text: Retrieve it from the machine manuals, since it is a written fact
Rely on the context window, since the student already said it
Raise the model's token limit so Monday's messages still fit
Save it to a note outside the window and load it next session

items.stem: A page of the laser cutter manual says only "Set the speed to 40%." Retrieval returns it for a question about the 3D printer. In one sentence, what is the likely cause, and what could fix it?
